clue.text: Work out what bad things fly!

parts.note: a machine that runs is working
forth means out, as in going forth
eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard
ills are misfortunes or bad things

explanation.surface: An exhortation to work out what nasty things flee from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like a phrase meaning solve or exercise, but splits into two pieces; 'fly' is the verb flee, not insects.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to flee hastily from danger, which is what flying from something means.

clue.text: Cats possibly seen under a French grating

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: un is French for a
Cats is an example of a stage show with songs

explanation.surface: A cat heard beneath a French grille, perhaps meowing in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' looks like animals but is the Lloyd Webber show; the definition is 'grating' in the sense of harsh to the ear, not a metal grille.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating sound is harsh and tuneless, lacking any melodic quality.

clue.text: Do without instead of work

parts.note: for can mean in place of, as in a substitute for
a machine that goes is one that works

explanation.surface: Doing without something rather than working for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up or abstain from it.

clue.text: Daily event one celebrates, interrupting trip

indicators.note: the words for one celebrating break into the word for trip

parts.note: a run is a short journey or outing
I is the Roman numeral one
to sing of something is to celebrate it

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates every day by breaking off a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise happens every morning, so it is an everyday occurrence.

clue.text: Layer cake missing top honours from here

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs

indicators.note: the top honours are taken out of the cake

parts.note: taken as the plain word
in card games the ace and king are the top honours, A and K

explanation.surface: A layer cake lacking its decoration, said by a baker to a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer cake' reads as one dessert but splits into an egg-layer and a cake; honours here are bridge's top cards, ace and king.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means from this place, as in 'get thee hence'.

clue.text: Impetuosity is like a fork — sensible at first

parts.note: a fork has prongs called tines, so something like it has tines

indicators.note: only the opening letter of sensible is used

explanation.surface: A rash claim that impetuosity resembles a fork, with sense coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetuosity is rushing in without thought, the same as rashness or haste.

clue.text: Look and see — neither finish at large

indicators.note: neither word may keep what follows, so those letters are dropped from both
the finish of each word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to look and see, with neither task completed.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped animal at large is free, unconfined and roaming.

clue.text: Gently cooked vegetable mostly consumed inside

indicators.note: the word for consumed goes within the shortened vegetable
the vegetable loses its last letter

parts.note: a swede is a root vegetable (rutabaga in the US)
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A vegetable lightly cooked and mostly eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: SWEDE is the British name for rutabaga; 'mostly' trims it to SWED.
explanation.definitionFit: In cookery, vegetables are sweated by heating them gently in fat so they soften without browning.

clue.text: 16 people here pick up large risk

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word for large so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: big means large
a bet is a gamble or risk

explanation.surface: Someone picking up a large risk, cross-referenced to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is SUSPENDED: a gallows is where people were hanged, so suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallows is where hanged people were left dangling, so it is where the suspended are found.

clue.text: Gizmo stripped down at Irish port

indicators.note: Gizmo is stripped of its outer letters, keeping the middle

explanation.surface: A gadget being dismantled down at an Irish harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish port' looks like one phrase, but the port is Turkish; Irish only gives IR.
explanation.definitionFit: Izmir, the former Smyrna, is a major Turkish seaport on the Aegean.

clue.text: Building material beginning to split with weight

indicators.note: only the first letter of split is taken

parts.note: and means together with
a stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds

explanation.surface: Construction material starting to crack under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: This sedimentary rock is widely quarried for building.

clue.text: Instrument bishop's playing in the near future

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; the 's reads as is, a link
an actor playing a role appears as that character
soon means before long

explanation.surface: A bishop will be performing on an instrument shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: This double-reed woodwind is a familiar orchestral instrument.

clue.text: Notable setter's positioned in space and time

indicators.note: the setter's possessive is placed inside space and time

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
the setter refers to themselves as I, so setter's is mine

explanation.surface: The compiler boasts of being located somewhere in space-time.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is 'I', so setter's gives MINE; EN is a typographic space.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notable is distinguished or prominent, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Sound of drain changes direction

indicators.note: the word for drain is said aloud

parts.note: a tax is a drain on resources

explanation.surface: The noise a plughole makes as the water swirls the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' looks like plumbing, but it is a burden: a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat tacks when it turns its bow through the wind onto a new course.

clue.text: Signals from coast include electronic chart

indicators.note: the word for coast takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the shore is the coast
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail
a map is a chart

explanation.surface: Signals sent from the coast carry an electronic chart.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a system of flag or arm signals for sending messages at a distance.

clue.text: South American writer, reportedly late, not in office right now

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the word for late is said aloud

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A South American author, rumoured dead, is out of office for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' is deceased, not tardy; it sounds like DED.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who is temporarily barred from their post is held out of office for the time being.

clue.text: Soviet worker has tank with over half missing repaired

indicators.note: fixed up, so these letters are put back together in a new order
over loses half its letters, keeping the first two

explanation.surface: A Soviet labourer has a tank, more than half of which is missing, mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over half missing' reads as 'more than half', but it means OVER with half gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexei Stakhanov was a Soviet miner held up as a model of outstanding productivity.

clue.text: Outlaw's daughter replacing books in Dutch language

indicators.note: the daughter abbreviation takes the place of the books inside the language

parts.note: Esperanto is an invented international language
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An outlaw's daughter swaps books written in Dutch for another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch language' looks like a unit, but Dutch is only D and the language is ESPERANTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate, reckless criminal of the Wild West is exactly an outlaw.

clue.text: Battle proposal a man carefully hides

indicators.note: the answer is concealed in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A man carefully conceals a marriage proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington defeated the French at this Spanish city in 1812 during the Peninsular War.

clue.text: Inventing nothing is ultimately generous

indicators.note: only the final letter of is is used

parts.note: lavish means generous or unstinting

explanation.surface: Creating nothing is ultimately a generous act.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish work copies others exactly, with no originality of its own.

clue.text: Business end of Stinger is aluminium fibre

indicators.note: the leading letter of Stinger, the end that does the work

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: The sharp tip of a sting is made of a metal fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from agave leaves, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Message Q?

definitions.meaning: a written communication sent by post
Q is one character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A cryptic message signed simply Q, as in a spy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A written note sent to someone, and also any single character of the alphabet such as Q.

clue.text: Gets book about mushroom

indicators.note: the book goes round the mushroom

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament
a cep is a porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a book about fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a point is to understand and agree with it, which is to take it on board.

clue.text: One leaving prison, avoiding French art heist

indicators.note: the French word is kept out of the one leaving prison

parts.note: a person who breaks out of jail is an escaper
es is French for art, as in tu es, thou art

explanation.surface: A convict breaking out shuns a robbery of French artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the archaic verb (thou art), so French art is ES, not paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a daring robbery or crime is the same as a heist.

clue.text: Threw one in outhouse

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone hurled one thing into the outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy something is to fling or toss it, as at a coconut shy.

clue.text: Yield when her VAT's collected

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up and assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A business's return when her sales tax is gathered in.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm's crop for the season is its yield.

clue.text: Played around, leaving Mark tied up

indicators.note: the mark abbreviation departs from the word for played around

parts.note: to romp is to play boisterously
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone fooled about, then left Mark bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roped is secured with cord, so tied up.

clue.text: Look after gnome and child to get over current collapse

indicators.note: the word for look follows the sprite

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous sprite, like a gnome
lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: the child is spread over the current symbol, surrounding it

parts.note: a son is a child
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone told to watch a garden gnome and a child through a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as babysit, but here 'after' is a placing instruction; I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: When something caves in on itself, as a building or star does, it falls inward.

clue.text: Tree in quiet street

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet
a lane is a narrow street

explanation.surface: A tree growing in a peaceful road.
explanation.definitionFit: The London plane is a common broadleaf tree of city streets.

clue.text: Crash a very old Danish two-wheeler

indicators.note: a crash smashes things, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A very old Dane has a smash on his bike.
explanation.definitionFit: This American motorcycle brand is an iconic two-wheeler.
